Björk, “All Is Full of Love” music video

Chris Cunningham’s video of two white robots with Björk’s features, assembled and kissing in a clinical white room.

Source
Wikipedia: All Is Full of Love

Style

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The video was directed by Chris Cunningham and premiered in April 1999; post-production was by Glassworks. Cunningham described a white environment with “a Japanese feel to it”. It won MTV Video Music Awards for Breakthrough Video and Best Special Effects in 2000 and was on permanent exhibition at the Museum of Modern Art. Wikipedia: All Is Full of Love.

Media Art Net describes two humanoid robots being assembled, kissing, and falling in love. Media Art Net.

Why it belongs

The cyborg is one of the style’s image motifs. This video shows its sincere, tender version around 1999: the machine as beautiful, not threatening.

It is close to the white, minimal side of the period and is useful as an edge case for the Y2K rubric.

Borrow

Pair white glossy surfaces with a cool, soft light to suggest a clean-room future.
